title: Origins and History of Hammond Model A/B3
body:
The Hammond Model A/B3 belongs to the 1935–1970s era and traces to Laurens Hammond.

The Telharmonium (1906) was the first electronic music; the theremin (1920) made it expressive and eerie. Laurens Hammond's tonewheel organ (1935) gave churches and jazz clubs the B-3; the Novachord (1939) previewed polyphonic synthesis. Postwar: the Clavioline, Ondes Martenot, and RCA Mark II (1957, the room-sized synth). Robert Moog's modular (1964) and Minimoog (1970) put synthesis in musicians' hands; ARP, EMS, and Oberheim followed. The Rhodes (1946/1965) and Wurlitzer defined electric piano; the Mellotron's tapes defined prog. Drum machines (Roland CR-78, TR-808 1980, LinnDrum 1982) mechanized rhythm; the Fairlight CMI (1979) and Synclavier sampled reality. MIDI (1983) let them all talk.

Within that longer story, Hammond Model A/B3: The 1935; the tonewheel's. The Hammond is the organ's electric.

title: How Hammond Model A/B3 Works
body:
Tonewheel organs spin magnetic wheels past pickups (additive synthesis with drawbars). Analog synths shape oscillator waveforms (saw/square) through filters (VCF) and amplifiers (VCA) steered by envelope generators (ADSR) — subtractive synthesis. The Mellotron plays back tape loops of real instruments per key. Drum machines sequence analog voices (808's booming kick is a bridged-T oscillator) or digital samples (LinnDrum). Samplers record sound into RAM and play it pitched across keys. MIDI carries note/control data at 31.25 kbaud between them all.

Applied to the Hammond Model A/B3 (1935–1970s, Laurens Hammond): The Hammond is the organ's electric.

The engineering principles above are exactly what made this class of technology practical: every unit is a working compromise between materials, energy, precision, and cost.

title: Anatomy of Hammond Model A/B3 — Components
body:
Every Hammond Model A/B3 is an assembly of the historical musical instruments family's standard parts:

• Oscillator (VCO/DCO) — Pitch source: saw, square, triangle, sine.
• Filter (VCF) — Subtractive tone shaping; the Moog ladder legend.
• Amplifier (VCA) — Loudness shaping per note.
• Envelope (ADSR) — Attack-decay-sustain-release articulation.
• LFO — Low-frequency modulation: vibrato, tremolo, filter sweeps.
• Keyboard / controller — CV/gate or MIDI note input.
• Tonewheels / tines / reeds — Electromechanical sound generation.
• Tape heads / loops — Mellotron/Chamberlin playback per key.
• Sequencer — Step programming of patterns (808's 16 steps).
• MIDI interface — 5-pin DIN; channels, clock, sync.

When examining a surviving Hammond Model A/B3, identify these parts in order: Oscillator (VCO/DCO), Filter (VCF), Amplifier (VCA), Envelope (ADSR), LFO, Keyboard / controller.

title: Historical Musical Instruments Glossary
body:
The working vocabulary of historical musical instruments:

• ADSR — Envelope stages shaping each note.
• VCO/VCF/VCA — Voltage-controlled oscillator/filter/amplifier.
• subtractive synthesis — Filtering harmonics from rich oscillators.
• additive synthesis — Stacking sine harmonics (tonewheel, Fairlight).
• FM synthesis — Chowning's method; the DX7's electric pianos.
• sampling — Recording reality into the instrument.
• MIDI — 1983 digital note/control standard.
• CV/gate — Analog control voltage + trigger; pre-MIDI.
• drawbars — Hammond's additive mixing sliders.
• Leslie speaker — Rotating horn/drum; the Hammond's swirl.
• tape loop — Mellotron's 8 seconds of orchestra per key.
• drum machine — Pattern-programmable rhythm; 808/909/Linn.

title: Collecting and Preserving Hammond Model A/B3

Minimoogs and 2600s are blue-chip — verify originality, recap power. Mellotrons need tape-loop love and a tech. Rhodes/Wurlitzers: tines and reeds tune; tolex wears. 808s/909s: check all voices and buttons; recap. MIDI retrofits add value if reversible.

For the Hammond Model A/B3 specifically: 1935's wheels: the 1935 — the 1955's B3.. Prioritize completeness and originality over shine; a working Hammond Model A/B3 with honest wear outranks a polished non-runner.

title: Hammond Model A/B3 Restoration Guide
body:
Recap power supplies first. Clean key contacts and sliders (DeoxIT). Calibrate oscillators and filters per service manual. Replace tantalum caps proactively. Keep away from heat; store with dust covers.

Restoration order for a Hammond Model A/B3: 1) document everything photographically before touching it; 2) stabilize (clean, de-corrode, free seized parts); 3) repair before replacing; 4) replace only what is missing or dangerous, marking replacements; 5) test under supervision. Never power an unrestored electrical music instrument record without a current-limited bring-up.
